terms.comment: A boy, and in the plural children of either sex (Lewis & Short: “orig. a child, whether boy or girl”). Puer in apposition is “as a child”: vidēbam puer, “I used to see as a boy”. A girl is puella (see girl).

terms.gloss: baby, small child who cannot yet talk
evidence: Cic. Div. 1.121: cum īnfāns esset (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: The diminutive of parvus, affectionate; parvī and parvulī are “little ones”.
Children as sons and daughters, never a child in general (see children).

phrases.latin: C. Duellium … redeuntem ā cēnā senem saepe vidēbam puer
phrases.english: as a child I often saw old Gaius Duilius coming home from dinner
because as a boy I played ball
